newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury edges higher after results.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury edges higher after results.

text.p: Shares in supermarket chain J. Sainsbury rose 6p to 361p in pre-market trading after half-year results at the top end of analyst forecasts, traders said.

Pre-tax profits fell to 393 from 456 million stg and compared with market expectations ranging from 383 to 396 million stg. The dividend payout was raised to 3.5 pence, up from 3.4 pence previously. Sainsbury said that current like-for-like sales growth in its supermarkets, before petrol sales, was now "in-line with sales inflation of three percent". It said supermarket gross margins were stable while in petrol they were improving.

"Everybody knew the figures were going to be poor and the range of forecasts had been moved down ahead of them. I suspect after these results people will be looking to downgrading their forecasts for the full year," said one analyst.

News that Dino Adriano will take over from Tom Vyner as chief executive of its core UK supermarkets division on March 8 rather than at the end of 1997 as previously planned helped the shares early on, said one analyst, though another was less convinced.
"That maybe the knee jerk reaction but it may not make that much difference, he's still pretty well unproven," he said.
"There are question marks about what they say on current trading - sales moving in-line with inflation is pretty disappointing considering they've introduced the loyalty card."
Sainsbury said its loyalty card, launched four months ago, was contributing between two and three percent of incremental sales, excluding the impact of Savercards last year.
And while Homebase's performance was as anticipated other areas were less impressive, said the analyst.
"Savacentre figures were worse than I expected and Shaw's was disappointing. They say it was down to store opening costs but there must have been other reasons for the disappointments."
"Comments from David Sainsbury that this year will be about "getting the basics right' doesn't sound very exciting," he added.

Sainsbury, which last week announced plans to launch financial services with Bank of Scotland, said there would be a further "major development" with its Reward loyalty card soon and that it looked forward to "a strong Christmas trading season."
